name: Norway
tagline: Free, close to home — and almost entirely in Norwegian
summary: Norway charges EU/EEA students no tuition, and your IB converts generously onto the Norwegian scale. The catch is language. Four of the biggest universities — NTNU, UiT, HVL and in practice UiB — offer no bachelor's degree taught in English at all. If you do not speak Norwegian, your realistic shortlist is about eight institutions and around fifteen programmes. If you are willing to reach B2 Norwegian, the entire free system opens up through one central application with ten ranked choices.
whyConsider: No tuition at public institutions for EU/EEA citizens — you pay only a semester fee of roughly NOK 850–1,000.
Danish SU travels here at the full udeboende rate, and Nordic study does not consume your Danish klippekort.
IB Maths AA SL on its own satisfies the Norwegian R1+R2 requirement, so engineering needs only Physics SL alongside it.
43–45 IB points converts to 60.0 karakterpoeng — the top of the Norwegian scale.
Genuinely distinctive niches: Arctic and marine biology at Nord, game development at INN, sport science at NIH.
watchOuts: NTNU, UiT and HVL state plainly that they offer no English-taught bachelor's degrees. UiB's three English-listed 'bachelors' are Norwegian-language degrees.
English-taught programmes apply direct to the institution and often close on 1 December 2026 — months before Danish or British norms, and before predicted grades are settled.
NMBU says explicitly that it does not offer conditional admission to applicants who finish their education after the deadline.
The Samordna opptak documentation deadline of 1 July falls before IB results are released on 6 July. You must arrange the IBO Request for Results Service with your IB coordinator.
Lånekassen is realistically closed to a school-leaver arriving from Denmark, and Norway offers no scholarships to EU/EEA bachelor students.
Living costs are high: the official student budget is NOK 15,488 per month, roughly €1,320.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No minimum point score for a full IB Diploma holder — holding the Diploma is itself the education requirement. A DP Course Results / IB Certificate needs more than 20 points, passed TOK and Extended Essay, completed CAS, and grade 3 or better in either 3 SL + 3 HL or 2 SL + 4 HL subjects.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Grade 3 or better is required in each subject used to meet a specific requirement. Mathematical Studies SL and Maths AI SL cover S1+S2. Maths AA SL, AA HL and AI HL all cover R1+R2. Physics SL covers Fysikk 1 and Physics HL covers Fysikk 1+2; the same SL/HL pattern applies to Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Economics and Design Technology.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: Total points (the 45-point scale, including TOK/EE bonus points) converts to Norwegian karakterpoeng: 43–45 = 60.0, 42 = 59.3, 41 = 58.6, 40 = 57.1, 38 = 54.3, 35 = 50.0, 32 = 45.7, 30 = 42.9, 28 = 40.0, 24 = 34.3, 20 = 26.0. Samordna opptak states the table applies to the current admission year and may change.
notes: That Maths AA SL alone satisfies R1+R2 is the single most favourable rule in Norway for IB students. In the Danish system the equivalent normally means Matematik A.
IB English at grade 3 or better satisfies the national English requirement — no IELTS or TOEFL needed.

The Norwegian language requirement does not apply to programmes taught in English (opptaksforskrifta § 3-8). Institutions do not apply this uniformly, though: NMBU requires Norwegian B2 for some admissions even on English-taught programmes.

Open question worth an email: a Danish student holding an IB Diploma from a Danish gymnasium sits between § 2-3 (Nordic education gives automatic GSK with no Norwegian test) and § 2-4 (IB is assessed as IB, needing Norwegian A or B). Samordna opptak treats IB as its own entry, which suggests § 2-4 governs. Write to sokerinfo@samordnaopptak.no before relying on the Nordic exemption.
Also unconfirmed: whether an IB Diploma earned abroad counts as a førstegangsvitnemål for the reserved quota. This materially affects how competitive you are.

deadlines.label: English-taught programmes, EU/EEA applicants (typical)
deadlines.notes: UiA opens 1 February and closes 1 March. NHH runs 1 January – 15 February 2027. Nord runs 1 February – 15 April.

deadlines.label: English-taught programmes, the early closers
deadlines.notes: UiO's Technology Systems and NMBU's International Environment and Development Studies both close on 1 December 2026, for everyone including EU citizens.

steps: Decide early whether you are applying in English or in Norwegian — they are two different systems with different deadlines, and you can use both.
For English-taught programmes, apply directly to each institution through its Søknadsweb portal. Check each deadline individually; they range from 1 December 2026 to 15 April 2027.

For Norwegian-taught programmes, register on Samordna opptak from 1 February 2027 and list up to ten choices in order of preference. A lower choice is dropped automatically once a higher one is offered.
Ask your IB coordinator to submit the IBO Request for Results Service in spring 2027 so your results reach Norway directly — the 1 July documentation deadline falls before results day.
Upload your IB diploma and transcript. No translation is needed for documents in English or a Scandinavian language.
Register with the police within three months of arriving, bringing your passport, EHIC and admission letter.
application.selectionNotes: Two quotas: a first-time-certificate quota competing on skolepoeng, and an ordinary quota competing on konkurransepoeng (which adds age points and up to two supplementary points). For autumn 2027 the procedural reforms bite — særskilt vurdering is abolished, ties are broken by lottery, and institutions may introduce their own ranking entrance tests — but age points, the current supplementary-point regime and the 50% first-time quota all survive. The bigger changes, including the removal of age points entirely, land in 2028.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Very limited — roughly fifteen programmes nationally. HK-dir lists 361 English-taught programmes across all levels, but these are overwhelmingly master's.
language.englishProof: IB English (A or B) at grade 3 or better satisfies the national requirement, as does English being your language of instruction. The national floor for test-takers is IELTS 5.0 or TOEFL iBT 60, but individual programmes set higher bars.
notes: Norwegian is not required for programmes taught in English, but it is required for everything else — which is most of the system.
Norwegian B2 can be documented through Norskprøven (B2 in all four skills) or Bergenstesten.

Danish and Norwegian are mutually intelligible in writing, so reaching B2 Norwegian is a far smaller undertaking for a Danish student than for most applicants. This is worth taking seriously — it unlocks the whole free system.

tuitionEuEea.value: None at public institutions. BI Norwegian Business School is private and charges NOK 106,400 per year even to EU/EEA students.

tuitionNonEu.value: Mandatory but no longer required to be cost-covering since 1 August 2026. Several institutions cut fees sharply: Nord and UiS now NOK 60,000–85,000, INN NOK 68,000, USN NOK 50,000–90,000. NTNU, UiO, UiB and HVL did not cut. UiO's 2027/28 rates are NOK 218,000 for science and technology and NOK 186,000 for humanities and social science.

livingCostMonthly.value: NOK 15,488 per month (about €1,320), or NOK 170,368 per year

notes: Every student pays a semester fee of roughly NOK 850–1,000. It buys the student ID, discounted transport, health services and gym access, and you cannot sit exams without it.

The figure of NOK 15,488 per month is formally the immigration authority's subsistence requirement for non-EEA students, but it is also the realistic cost of living and the right number for a Danish student to budget against.

funding: Danish SU at the udeboende rate — DKK 7,426 per month before tax in 2026. Nordic study is treated like studying in Denmark and does not consume your Danish higher-education klippekort.

Lånekassen, the Norwegian loan fund, requires either permanent residence, five years in Norway, or worker status with at least ten hours a week alongside your studies. A 19-year-old arriving straight from gymnasium does not qualify — though taking a part-time job is a genuine route in.
There are no Norwegian government scholarships for EU/EEA bachelor students. Study in Norway says so outright.
workRights: No restriction for EU/EEA students. Non-EU students on a first-time permit may work 20 hours a week during term and full-time in holidays.
residency: No residence permit needed. Register with the police within three months of arrival, bringing your passport or national ID, your EHIC or private insurance covering the whole stay, your admission letter and a declaration of sufficient funds. After six months you report a move and receive a national identity number.
housing: Run by the Samskipnad (student welfare organisation) in each city — SiO in Oslo — and funded by the semester fee. Applications are accepted year-round and offers go out continuously. Oslo, Bergen and Trondheim all have shortages at the August intake, and Oslo's private market is the main reason Norway is expensive despite free tuition. Apply the day your offer arrives.
healthcare: Bring your Danish EHIC. It covers medically necessary care from public providers on the same terms as a tourist. Once you are registered as resident with a national identity number you get care on the same basis as Norwegians, including a fastlege (assigned GP). Helsenorge recommends private insurance on top, particularly for repatriation. Taking a job generally makes you a member of folketrygden — check with NAV.

institutions.name: University of Agder
institutions.englishBachelors: 4 — Academic Esports (Grimstad), Classical Music Performance, Electronic Music, English
institutions.note: The best public-university option in Norway for an IB student who wants an English-taught bachelor's — four genuine choices, AACSB-accredited business school, and a 1 March deadline rather than 1 December.

institutions.name: BI Norwegian Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Business Administration (BBA), Data Science for Business, Digital Business
institutions.note: The widest choice of English-taught bachelors in Norway, triple-crown accredited — but private, and the one institution on this list where EU/EEA students pay tuition: NOK 106,400 a year.

institutions.name: Inland Norway University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Game Art and Animation (Hamar), Game Technology (Hamar), Philosophy, Politics and Economics (Lillehammer)
institutions.note: The surprise of the Norwegian list — two game-development degrees and a PPE, all in English, all free for EU/EEA students. Hamar is a recognised Norwegian games-education cluster. INN gained full university status in 2024.

institutions.name: Norwegian School of Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — BSc in Business, Economics and Data Science
institutions.note: Norway's most selective business school — roughly 20% acceptance, triple-crown accredited, and about 40% of students go on exchange. Free for EU/EEA. The EU/EEA window closes 15 February 2027.

institutions.name: Norwegian University of Life Sciences
institutions.note: Home to the only veterinary education in Norway. For an IB student drawn to ESS, biology and global development this is one of very few real entry points — but the deadline is 1 December 2026 and NMBU does not make conditional offers.

institutions.name: University of Oslo
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Technology Systems: Science and Engineering (Kjeller campus)
institutions.note: Norway's oldest and most prestigious university — but for an IB student without Norwegian there is exactly one bachelor door, and it closes on 1 December 2026.

institutions.name: Nord University
institutions.englishBachelors: 1–2 — BSc Biology (Bodø) confirmed; Acting and Artistic Production listed elsewhere but unconfirmed
institutions.note: The English-taught BSc Biology in Bodø is genuinely distinctive — Arctic and aquatic biology above the Arctic Circle, free for EU/EEA students. Documentation can be extended to 1 July, which helps an IB applicant.

institutions.name: Oslo National Academy of the Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Classical Ballet only; the other nine bachelors are taught in Norwegian
institutions.note: A tiny, fiercely selective conservatoire outside the national admission system. The only English door is Classical Ballet, audition-driven, closing at the end of February.

institutions.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: None. NTNU states plainly that it offers no bachelor's degrees taught in English.
institutions.note: Norway's engineering powerhouse and its largest university, with a Nobel-winning neuroscience institute — and completely inaccessible at bachelor level without Norwegian B2. Worth planning towards as a master's destination.

institutions.name: University of Bergen
institutions.englishBachelors: None in practice. UiB's English filter returns three bachelors, but all three are Norwegian-language degrees with English components.
institutions.note: World-class for marine and climate science. Treat it as a master's destination — the bachelor listing in English is misleading.

institutions.name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
institutions.englishBachelors: None. UiT states it currently offers no bachelor programmes taught in English.
institutions.note: The world's northernmost university and unique for Arctic, marine and space science — but bachelor entry is closed to non-Norwegian speakers. Master's applications open 1 February 2027.

institutions.name: Norwegian School of Sport Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: None indicated — bachelor teaching is in Norwegian; English provision starts at master's level.
institutions.note: Ranked among the top three sport-science schools in the world since 2017. Bachelor entry goes through Samordna opptak in Norwegian.

institutions.name: University of Stavanger
institutions.englishBachelors: Around 1 — Dance; language of instruction not confirmed.
institutions.note: Norway's energy-industry university, in the country's oil capital. Cut its non-EEA fees sharply from August 2026.

institutions.name: Oslo Metropolitan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Unclear — the programme filter indicates one, but it could not be identified. Email international@oslomet.no before assuming.
institutions.note: Large and professionally oriented, with around 20,000 students. Cut its product-design fee for non-EEA students from NOK 418,000 to NOK 95,000 in August 2026.
